expectations_used.clarify: Pins down what the failing test actually asserts before editing — that a ticket arriving at the first minute of the evening belongs to the incoming agent — and asks the interviewer which shift owns a minute that two windows appear to share, rather than assuming the test is wrong.
expectations_used.approach: Names a mechanism out loud before changing code — e.g. that the outgoing agent survives the on-shift filter at the boundary minute and then beats the incoming agent on the fewest-open-tickets rank key — instead of pointing vaguely at 'the shift code'.
expectations_used.communicate: Keeps a running account while reading roster.py, policy.py and router.py, saying which candidate explanation each observation rules out — skill match, concurrency cap, tenure bar, rank ordering — and announcing each move from the failing test to the filter to the ranking rather than working silently.
expectations_used.implement: Corrects the boundary in minutes_into_shift so an agent stops being eligible at their shift end minute, matching the half-open Shift.covers, and leaves the rank key, the tenure bar and the tests untouched.
expectations_used.verify: Re-runs the full suite after the fix, confirms the evening-handover test passes, and checks the wrap-past-midnight and coverage-report tests still pass rather than stopping at the one assertion.
expectations_used.reflect: Explains that the defect was a disagreement between two on-shift implementations — the inclusive comparison in policy versus the half-open Shift.covers — and why the load-based ranking is what turned that overlap into the wrong agent, not merely that the assertion is now green.

summary: The candidate asked to be pointed at the bug file, was redirected twice by the interviewer, and only at the very end stated a hypothesis about an inclusive-vs-half-open shift boundary that is close to the actual planted bug — but they ended the session immediately after, before tracing it to code, attempting a fix, or verifying anything.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate opened by asking the interviewer which file the bug was in rather than reading the failing test output themselves, which the interviewer rightly declined to answer. The later spec question about inclusive vs half-open shift windows was a genuinely good question, but it came without any grounding in observed test output or code they had cited, so it reads as a guess dressed as a clarifying question rather than a resolution of a stated ambiguity.

When pressed, the candidate articulated a specific mechanism — an inclusive-vs-half-open mismatch in the eligibility filter letting the outgoing agent survive and win on load — which is remarkably close to the actual planted bug. However this came only after two deflected questions and immediately before the session ended, so it was never acted upon or tested.

For most of the five-minute session the candidate said very little: two short questions over 240 seconds, then a single dense claim. There is no running narration of what they read, tried, or ruled out beyond the one retrospective sentence at 276s, so an interviewer could not follow their path as it happened.
No editor events were recorded at all and the candidate never described making or attempting a code change before ending the session, so there is nothing to assess against the stated approach.
The session ended immediately after the hypothesis was stated and before any fix was attempted, let alone verified; no test run or check was described.

The candidate was asked directly what evidence supported their claim about the inclusive/half-open mismatch and instead of answering, the session ended with them clicking End Session, leaving the mechanism unconnected to any cited code or test output.
